protocol: blocked 5-fold: fit blocks<5, cal blocks>=5, test blocks%5==k; identical folds for every representation and every model

decision_rules.A1: prior-free detector within 0.02 AUROC of the gate => gate is not the contribution; justify by joint refuse+cover behaviour
decision_rules.B1: exact-set > 0.10 on held-out composites for any model/rep => rewrite 'not an artefact of one model family' as 'one linear model family'
decision_rules.B2: LDA(svd) balanced accuracy must not move between raw and white (invertible linear map); > 0.02 means the feature map is broken and Part B is void. Penalised learners are scale-sensitive and standardised in both arms, so their raw-vs-white gap is a result, not a bug signal
decision_rules.B3: 'prior helps across model classes' requires a gain averaged over the non-invariant classes on tea AND the same direction on cinnamon
decision_rules.C1: if a self-supervised representation reaches exact-set > 0.10 on held-out composites for any model class, Section 3.10's 'the representation is not the bottleneck' is confined to discrimination and may not be quoted for attribution; if SSL matches the analytic representations on T1 but stays at or below them on T2, Sections 3.10 and 3.3 collapse into one statement - learned representations buy no attribution either

partA.gate_definition: tau = (1-alpha)(1+1/n) quantile of the detector score on CALIBRATION SINGLES; flag = score > tau; test scores are divided by their own fold tau so the five folds are poolable and 1.0 is the operating point
partA.attribution_engine: fixed for every arm: whitened dictionary conformal set at alpha=0.1 plus argmin point attribution; only the refusal rule varies

partA.pool_note: held_out_adulterant: used_fit == pub_fit == the whole fit block, so the *_pub twins are the same computation as their non-pub originals and are not listed twice (measured: ours_gate 0.949 == ours_gate_pub 0.949). held_out_composite: the pools really differ, both families are reported.

train_rule: Part A keeps the manuscript's three-way split (dictionary from fit, thresholds from calibration). Part B baselines train on fit + calibration indices, i.e. on more labelled spectra than the paper's own engine consumes - the no-straw-man rule.
nls_row: ORACLE: best exact-set over the whole ladder, threshold read off the test composites - an upper bound, not a claim
scaling_rule: per-channel StandardScaler fitted on each arm's own training rows for the scale-sensitive learners above, in EVERY representation; LDA(svd), the trees, the torch arms (which standardise internally) and the dictionary arms are left unscaled because their invariance or their metric semantics is exactly what is under test
nls_cal_row: quotable NLS arm: dictionary from fit singles, relative cut from [0.05, 0.1, 0.15, 0.2, 0.25, 0.3, 0.35, 0.45] chosen as the smallest whose singleton-support accuracy on calibration singles is >= 0.9
torch_device: cpu (2.15.0+cpu) for Parts A and B; Part C and the cinnamon cross-check on cuda (2.15.0+cu132) - see run_log

partA_note: partA is the 03:34 re-run of the same code path with four extra published-pool prior-free arms (hotelling_t2_pub, spe_q_pub, ocsvm_pub, ae_resid_pub); every arm that existed in the earlier run reproduces field for field (846 shared leaf values, 1 difference and it is the detectors list itself). The *_pub twins are dropped from held_out_adulterant on purpose: there used_fit == pub_fit, so they were the same computation as their originals. ocsvm/ocsvm_pub report arm_absent rather than vanishing: -score_samples is negative on tea, so tau<=0 in 5/5 folds.
